translations.literal: Moreover, a successor may be strict in personal integrity and diligent in routine affairs yet unclear in far-reaching strategy, and may not fail to be self-willed and opinionated — would he willingly yield in everything?
translations.idiomatic: A successor might be upright and diligent yet lack strategic vision, insist on his own way, and refuse to yield on everything?

sentences.zh: 官文心無成見，兼隸旗籍，每有大事，正可藉其言以伸所請。

translations.literal: Guan Wen has no fixed prejudices and is also of banner registration; whenever there is a major matter, one can just borrow his words to advance one's requests.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen has no fixed prejudices and, as a bannerman, can speak for you on major matters at court.

sentences.zh: 其失僅在私費奢豪，誠於事有濟，歲糜十萬金供之，未為失計。

translations.literal: His faults lie only in private extravagance; if he truly helps affairs succeed, spending a hundred thousand taels a year to support him is not a mistaken plan.
translations.idiomatic: His fault is only private extravagance. If he truly advances the cause, spending a hundred thousand taels a year on him is no bad bargain.

sentences.zh: 至一二私人，可容，容之；

translations.literal: As for one or two private associates, if tolerable, tolerate them;
translations.idiomatic: As for one or two private associates, tolerate them if you can;

sentences.zh: 不可，則以事劾去之。

translations.literal: if not tolerable, impeach and remove them on grounds of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: if not, impeach and remove them on specific grounds.

sentences.zh: 彼意氣素平，必無忤也。

translations.literal: His temperament has always been even; there will certainly be no offense.
translations.idiomatic: His temperament is even; he will not take offense.

sentences.zh: 」林翼大悟。

translations.literal: " Linyi was greatly enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu Linyi was greatly enlightened.

sentences.zh: 及林翼歿，督撫不相能，官文劾嚴樹森去之；

translations.literal: When Linyi died, governor-general and governor could not work together; Guan Wen impeached Yan Shusen and had him removed;
translations.idiomatic: After Hu Linyi died, governor and governor-general clashed; Guan Wen impeached Yan Shusen and had him removed;

sentences.zh: 而曾國荃又劾官文去之。

translations.literal: and Zeng Guoquan in turn impeached Guan Wen and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: and Zeng Guoquan in turn impeached Guan Wen and had him removed as well.

sentences.zh: 官文晚節建樹不能如曩時，然林翼非官文之虛己推誠，亦無以成大功，世故兩賢之。

translations.literal: Guan Wen's achievements in his later years could not match his earlier days, yet without Linyi's emptying himself and extending sincerity to Guan Wen, great success could not have been achieved; the world therefore esteems both as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen's later achievements did not match his earlier record, yet without Hu Linyi's sincere deference to him, great success would not have been possible; posterity therefore esteems both men.

sentences.zh: 孫興恩，襲伯爵。

translations.literal: Sun Xingen inherited the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xingen inherited the earldom.

sentences.zh: 文煜，字星岩，費莫氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Wen Yu, courtesy name Xingyan, of the Feimo clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yu, whose courtesy name was Xingyan, belonged to the Feimo clan of the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 由官學生授太常寺庫使，累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: From the Imperial Academy he was appointed storekeeper of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A graduate of the Imperial Academy, he became storekeeper of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and rose to director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 出為直隸霸昌道、四川按察使。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Baxing circuit intendant of Zhili and provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Baxing circuit intendant in Zhili and surveillance commissioner in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，遷江寧布政使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, he was transferred to administration commissioner of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he was transferred to administration commissioner of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 時江寧已陷賊，文煜從琦善江北大營。

translations.literal: At the time Jiangning had already fallen to rebels; Wen Yu followed Qishan at the Jiangbei Grand Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning had already fallen, and Wen Yu joined Qishan at the Jiangbei headquarters.

sentences.zh: 四年，琦善歿於揚州，所部練勇及江北糧台事宜，命文煜接辦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Qishan died at Yangzhou; the trained braves under his command and matters of the Jiangbei grain depot were ordered transferred to Wen Yu to take over.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 Qishan died at Yangzhou, and Wen Yu took over his trained braves and the Jiangbei grain depot.

sentences.zh: 五年春，粵匪由瓜洲東竄沙頭港，文煜遣勇擊之，賊由對岸扎簰爭渡，偕水師以大砲合擊，賊退瓜洲。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, Cantonese rebels fled east from Guazhou to Shatou Harbor; Wen Yu dispatched braves to attack them. The rebels on the opposite bank lashed rafts to compete in crossing; together with the naval force they struck with great cannon in combined attack, and the rebels withdrew to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1855 Taiping rebels fled from Guazhou to Shatou Harbor. Wen Yu sent troops to attack them. When rebels lashed rafts to cross from the opposite bank, he and the navy drove them back to Guazhou with heavy cannon.

sentences.zh: 文煜以沙頭港為裡下河門戶，賊所必爭，築土城砲台，疏請添募練勇守禦，從之。

translations.literal: Wen Yu regarded Shatou Harbor as the gateway to the Lixia River region, which rebels would necessarily contest; he built earthen walls and batteries and memorialized requesting additional recruitment of trained braves for defense; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yu saw Shatou Harbor as the gateway to the Lixia River region and a point rebels would contest. He built walls and batteries and memorialized for more trained braves to defend it; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而賊踞揚州，窺裡下河，文煜擊之於萬安橋，大有斬獲，賊勢乃挫。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels held Yangzhou and eyed the Lixia River region; Wen Yu attacked them at Wan'an Bridge with many kills and captures, and rebel momentum was checked.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels held Yangzhou and threatened the Lixia River region, Wen Yu attacked them at Wan'an Bridge with heavy casualties on their side, checking their momentum.

sentences.zh: 七年，調江蘇布政使，治江南大營糧台。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to administration commissioner of Jiangsu and managed the grain depot of the Jiangnan Grand Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he was transferred to administration commissioner of Jiangsu and managed supplies for the Jiangnan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 以支給撙節，為軍中所不便，提督和春劾其拘泥，命來京候另簡用。

translations.literal: Because his disbursements were frugal and economical, which was inconvenient for the army, provincial military commissioner He Chun impeached him for rigidity; he was ordered to come to the capital to await another appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His frugal disbursements inconvenienced the army, and provincial military commissioner He Chun impeached him for rigidity. He was ordered to Beijing to await reassignment.

sentences.zh: 尋授直隸布政使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed administration commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed administration commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 九年，英兵犯大沽，為僧格林沁擊退。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, British troops invaded Dagu and were repelled by Sengge Rinchen.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 British forces attacked Dagu and were repelled by Sengge Rinchen.

sentences.zh: 戰後將議撫，命文煜從總督恆福赴北塘相機辦理。

translations.literal: After the battle pacification was to be discussed; Wen Yu was ordered to follow Governor Hengfu to Beitang to handle matters as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle the court prepared to negotiate peace and ordered Wen Yu to accompany Governor Hengfu to Beitang.

sentences.zh: 尋擢山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 捻匪圍曹縣，分黨擾安陵，檄曹州鎮總兵郝上庠合師內外夾擊，解曹州圍，安陵賊亦退。

translations.literal: Nian bandits besieged Caoxian and split into factions to harass Anling; he ordered Caozhou garrison commander Hao Shangxiang to join forces inside and outside in pincer attack, lifting the siege of Caozhou; the Anling rebels also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian bandits besieged Caoxian and raided Anling, he ordered Hao Shangxiang to attack from inside and outside, lifting the siege of Caozhou and driving off the Anling rebels.

sentences.zh: 十年，捻匪又竄單縣，分擾嶧縣得勝徬，遣將擊走之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Nian bandits again fled into Shan county and split to harass Desheng Pang in Yi county; he dispatched generals who drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 Nian bandits again entered Shan county and raided Desheng Pang in Yi county; he sent generals who drove them off.

sentences.zh: 英法聯軍踞砲台，文煜遣兵扼利津，自駐濰縣韓亭以防陸路北犯。

translations.literal: The British-French allied armies held the batteries; Wen Yu dispatched troops to hold Lijin and personally stationed at Hanting in Weixian to guard against a land-route invasion from the north.
translations.idiomatic: When the Anglo-French allies held the forts, Wen Yu posted troops at Lijin and stationed himself at Hanting in Weixian to block a northern land advance.

sentences.zh: 尋敵船北駛犯北塘，文煜分軍入衛，駐通州，自率眾赴濟寧剿捻匪。

translations.literal: Soon afterward enemy ships sailed north and invaded Beitang; Wen Yu divided troops to enter the capital guard, stationed at Tongzhou, and personally led a force to Jining to suppress Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy ships sailed north to Beitang, Wen Yu sent troops to guard the capital approaches, stationed at Tongzhou, and personally led forces to Jining against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署直隸總督，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he served as acting governor-general of Zhili and soon received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he served as acting governor-general of Zhili and was soon formally appointed.

sentences.zh: 時和議既成，穆宗回鑾，畿輔馬賊四起，久未淨絕，屢詔責文煜搜捕。

translations.literal: At the time peace had been concluded and the Muzong Emperor returned to the capital; mounted bandits rose everywhere in the capital region and long went unextinguished; repeated edicts charged Wen Yu to search and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had been concluded and the emperor returned to Beijing, but mounted bandits plagued the capital region for years. The court repeatedly ordered Wen Yu to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，坐山東降賊張錫珠等擾畿南督剿不力，褫職，戍軍台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, on account of the Shandong surrendered bandit Zhang Xizhu and others harassing the southern capital region while he supervised pursuit and suppression ineffectively, he was stripped of office and exiled to the military colony.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was dismissed and exiled to the military colony for failing to suppress Zhang Xizhu and other surrendered Shandong bandits who raided the southern capital region.

sentences.zh: 二年，僧格林沁奏調赴營差遣，尋授鑲黃旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: In the second year, Sengge Rinchen memorialized to transfer him to camp for assignment; soon afterward he was appointed vice commandant of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 Sengge Rinchen requested his transfer to headquarters, and he was soon made vice commandant of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 三年，命赴甘肅慶陽督辦糧台，以病請解職回旗。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was ordered to Gansu Qingyang to supervise the grain depot; on account of illness he requested release from office and return to his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he was ordered to Qingyang, Gansu, to supervise supplies but resigned on grounds of illness and returned to his banner.

sentences.zh: 七年，起授正藍旗漢軍都統，尋出為福州將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was raised and appointed commandant of the Manchu Plain Blue Banner Chinese Brigade; soon afterward he went out as general of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he was restored as commandant of the Manchu Plain Blue Banner Chinese Brigade and soon posted as general of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，兼署閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he concurrently served as acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he also served as acting governor-general of Fujian-Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，日本兵船窺伺台灣，偕總督​​李鶴年、船政大臣疏陳防務。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Japanese warships watched for an opportunity regarding Taiwan; together with Governor Li Henian and the naval affairs minister he memorialized on coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1874, when Japanese warships threatened Taiwan, he memorialized on coastal defense with Governor Li Henian and the naval affairs minister.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，入覲，留京授內大臣、鑲白旗漢軍都統、左都御史，擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu, he came to court for audience, remained in the capital, was appointed inner court minister, commandant of the Manchu Bordered White Banner Chinese Brigade, and left censor-in-chief, and was promoted to minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1877 he came to court, remained in Beijing, and was appointed inner court minister, commandant of the Bordered White Banner Chinese Brigade, left censor-in-chief, and minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 七年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was made assisting Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he was made assisting Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 九年，充總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he served as supervising minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 he served as supervising minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜武英殿大學士，以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Brilliance and requested retirement on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Brilliance and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子少保，諡文達。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wenda.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督曾國荃等奏文煜咸豐中孤軍捍賊，保全裡下河，請於揚州建專祠，允之。

translations.literal: Liangjiang governor-general Zeng Guoquan and others memorialized that during Xianfeng Wen Yu had defended alone against rebels and preserved the Lixia River region, requesting a special shrine at Yangzhou; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Liangjiang governor-general Zeng Guoquan and others memorialized that during the Xianfeng era Wen Yu had held off rebels alone and preserved the Lixia River region, and a special shrine at Yangzhou was approved.

sentences.zh: 子志顏，理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhiyan was vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiyan became vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 論曰：桂良以帝室葭莩，與聞軍國，數膺議和之使，無所折衝。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Gui Liang, through imperial kinship by marriage, took part in military and state affairs and repeatedly received missions to negotiate peace, yet achieved no diplomatic success.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary observes that Gui Liang, as an imperial in-law, took part in military and state affairs and repeatedly negotiated peace without diplomatic success.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟從僧格林沁勦賊防夷，曾著勞勚。

translations.literal: Rui Lin followed Sengge Rinchen in suppressing rebels and guarding against foreigners and once rendered distinguished labor.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Lin followed Sengge Rinchen in suppressing rebels and resisting foreigners and once rendered distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 文煜亦處兵間，無功可錄。

translations.literal: Wen Yu also was amid warfare, with no merit worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yu also served amid warfare, with little merit worth recording.

sentences.zh: 官文雖無過人之才，推賢讓能，奠安江漢，與曾國籓、胡林翼和衷規畫，竟完戡定之功。

translations.literal: Although Guan Wen had no surpassing talent, by promoting the worthy and yielding to the able he settled the Jiang and Han regions; working in harmony with Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi in planning, he finally completed the achievement of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Though Guan Wen lacked surpassing talent, he promoted worthy men, secured the Yangtze heartland, and planned in harmony with Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi to complete the pacification.

sentences.zh: 茅土同膺，旂常並煥，豈諸人所可並語哉？

translations.literal: They alike received fiefdoms and enfeoffment; their banners and records shine together — how can they be spoken of on the same level as the others?
translations.idiomatic: They alike received fiefs and honors; their banners shine together in the historical record — how can they be compared with the others?
